Article Title: Late-arriving grooms put on notice as Kashmir's wedding chefs set 10 pm deadline for wazwan
Article Text:

Kashmir's traditional wedding chefs, popularly known as 'waza', have decided to stop serving the elaborate multi-course wazwan after 10 pm, citing long working hours and poor treatment at wedding functions.The decision was taken unanimously at a meeting held at a marriage hall in the Rajouri Kadal area of Srinagar. The chefs said they had been forced to work under difficult conditions for years, particularly because wedding feasts often get delayed by the late arrival of the groom and his relatives.Ghulam Nabi Waza, president of the Kashmir Waza Association, said the community had remained silent about its working conditions for too long."It takes several hours to prepare the dishes, and usually we work late into the night. Then we are expected to start serving lunch from around 1 pm till 6 pm, which is followed by dinner, which starts well into the night," Waza told news agency PTI.He explained that the situation becomes even more difficult when chefs are hired to prepare food at the bride's house. They often have to wait until the groom and his wedding party arrive, sometimes well past midnight, before they can begin serving the feast."There have been incidents where the maulvi left without solemnising the nikah because the groom did not turn up till 1 am. We are also humans. So we now set the 10 pm deadline," Waza said.Waza also criticised the growing trend of guests arriving late for wedding celebrations and urged people to change what he described as a bad habit."There are so many people attached with the wazwan, and they too have the right to dignified working hours," he added.Other chefs at the meeting also raised concerns about how they are treated by wedding hosts. One of them said they are often not given proper arrangements to rest despite working for long hours."For example, we are not provided a proper place to sleep. We work long hours and need some time to rest before we prepare ourselves for the next day's gruelling routine. The hosts should take care of that aspect," the chef said.
Article Summary: Kashmir's traditional wedding chefs, popularly known as 'waza', have decided to stop serving the elaborate multi-course wazwan after 10 pm. The decision was taken unanimously at a meeting held at a marriage hall in the Rajouri Kadal area of Srinagar. The chefs said they had been forced to work under difficult conditions.

Article Title: Chemical-free crackers: RSS chief extols traditional Diwali practices as severe pollution chokes Delhi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has defended traditional Diwali practices, saying they were rooted in science and served environmental purposes, including eliminating insects and purifying the air.His remarks come amid continuing concerns over air pollution in major Indian cities.Addressing a gathering in Nagpur, Bhagwat said firecrackers used in earlier times were free of harmful chemicals and helped eliminate insects. He also cited the practice of lighting lamps fuelled by ghee, saying it helped purify the atmosphere.“There was science behind these traditional practices,” he said, invoking the phrase “Vatavaran shuddh, jeevan shuddh” (a clean environment leads to a pure life).The RSS chief's comments come against the backdrop of worsening air quality in Delhi and several other metropolitan cities, where firecracker use during Diwali has remained a contentious issue. Pollution from fireworks, along with other sources, has repeatedly raised concerns over their environmental and health impact.Bhagwat also spoke about the cultural significance of Diwali, noting that the five-day festival is celebrated across the world and brings people together to exchange greetings and good wishes.He further said that 'dharma' serves to unite society and that women often possess a deeper understanding of it than men.Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years, with the average Air Quality Index (AQI) at 376.The situation remained largely unchanged on Monday morning, with the AQI settling at 371 at 10 am as a blanket of smog and fog covered the city, news agency PTI reported.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat said firecrackers used in earlier times were free of harmful chemicals and helped eliminate insects. He also cited the practice of lighting lamps fuelled by ghee, saying it helped purify the atmosphere. His remarks come amid continuing concerns over air pollution in major Indian cities.

Article Title: What made Sonia Gandhi turn down PM post after UPA’s 2004 victory? Memoir revisits moment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has revealed what went through her mind when she decided against becoming prime minister after the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) won the 2004 Lok Sabha elections.In her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recalls how she eventually listened to her "inner voice" and decided to turn down the top post, despite initially being expected to lead the government. She also explains why she chose Manmohan Singh to become prime minister, describing him as a leader of "unquestionable" integrity with a deep understanding of governance.The memoi revisits the crucial political decision that shaped the UPA government's first term. Sonia also shares details of the discussions with senior Congress leaders and her final conversation with her son, Rahul Gandhi, before announcing her decision.Also Read| 'I'd quake in my seat': Sonia Gandhi recalls Indira Gandhi's temper, early days as bride in memoir Sharing an excerpt from the memoir in an article published by The Indian Express, Sonia Gandhi recalled the moment she finally resolved not to become prime minister."My mind suddenly cleared itself of the last shreds of doubt. “Sonia, be true to yourself,” I could hear myself say.“You’ve always known it. Just leave it!” From Belonging - on the decision not to become Prime Minister," she wrote in a post on X.In the book, she describes how she woke up a few hours later and went straight to Rahul's room to tell him about her decision."I woke up in a few hours, went straight to my son’s room, and knocked on the door. “I’ve made up my mind. I’m going to stick to my stand,” I told him. He stepped up to me and with his arms around me said, “It’s the right decision.”"The CPP President also recalls returning to the Congress Parliamentary Party meeting after making up her mind."I enter the hall to thunderous applause. The members of Par­liament stand up in their places, thumping their palms on the wooden ledges in front of them. I find my place at the centre of the long table for the leaders of the party and remain standing till someone gestures for them to stop, and we all take our seats," she wrote.Also Read| 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir After deciding against taking the top post, Sonia had to identify someone who could lead the new government. She says several senior Congress leaders were qualified for the position, but Manmohan Singh stood out."There were several senior colleagues, seasoned and qualified for the post, who would have been more than willing to accept it but amongst all of them was one who had long been in my sight as a person above reproach, and possessed a deep and consummate understanding of governance. That was Dr Manmohan Singh, a member of the Congress Working Committee," she writes.Sonia points to Singh's experience as finance minister in the early 1990s, when he introduced economic reforms under the government of then prime minister PV Narasimha Rao.She also believed his appointment would reassure people about the UPA's economic policies, particularly as the alliance was supported by the Communist parties."He was not allied to any camp in the party. Over a period of time, the Congress had been painted as being left of centre, and our government would now be supported by the Communist parties as well. I thought Dr Manmohan Singh would assuage the doubts of many about our ability to manage and continue the policies that had been begun years ago," she says.Sonia also recalls Manmohan Singh's personal journey, from a village in Punjab, now in Pakistan, to the universities of Oxford and Cambridge. She describes him as a hardworking scholar and technocrat who had overcome considerable hardship."Aside from all his accomplishments as a scholar and technocrat, what I knew best about Dr Singh was that he had a kind and compassionate heart, and his integrity unquestionable," she writes.She says she was convinced that the country would be in safe hands under his leadership. After consulting senior colleagues, she proposed his name. They did not oppose the choice.Manmohan Singh was approached privately about taking up the position. Although he initially declined, the CPP President says he was eventually persuaded to accept it.Sonia Gandhi also recounts the events of May 18, 2004, when she went to Rashtrapati Bhawan to stake the UPA's claim to form the government. She was accompanied by Singh.Recalling her arrival, she describes an emotional moment as she walked through the building where she had earlier visited with her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi."I felt a sudden surge of emotion as our cars pulled up at the entrance. I'd been there many times before with my mother-in-law and with Rajiv, but this time I was walking through the long, dark corridors of Rashtrapati Bhawan for a different purpose," she writes.After the meeting, the two returned to her residence at 10, Janpath. Sonia Gandhi says she did not discuss the prime ministership with Singh, who, like everyone else, assumed she would take the post."We returned from Rashtrapati Bhawan to my home at 10, Janpath. I saw Dr Singh to his car. There had been no discussion about the prime ministership between the two of us on the drive back nor had there been before that. I said nothing to him even now. He had quite naturally assumed, like everyone else, that it would be me," she recalls.Sonia Gandhi has recalled how Pranab Mukherjee hinted at his "long-held desire" to become prime minister during a 2010 conversation, when he suggested that "it was time for a change at the top", according to her newly released memoir.Rejecting criticism that she was a "back seat driver" during the UPA years, Sonia said she respected Manmohan Singh's position as prime minister and believed it was her duty to defer to him, even when they disagreed."Further. I was determined not to be under any circumstance the cause of a misunderstanding that could give our opponents occasion to rejoice and weaken our government," she writes in the book, released on Tuesday.Also Read| ‘Not a political book, but a personal one’: Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release Belonging: A Journey of Love traces Sonia Gandhi's life from her childhood in post-war Italy to her marriage to Rajiv Sonia Gandhi and her eventual move to India.Born in Italy, she was 19 and studying in Cambridge, England, when she met Rajiv in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968. The memoir recounts her introduction to Indira Gandhi and her efforts to adjust to life in India, including learning Hindi, wearing saris and adapting to Indian food and culture.It also revisits the personal tragedies that shaped her life, including the death of Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.Among the most personal accounts is her recollection of the night Rajiv was assassinated in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, on May 21, 1991. She recalls how their daughter Priyanka broke the news to her and how she struggled to accept that her husband was dead.The memoir also recounts Rahul's concerns about his father's security. Two months before the assassination, Rahul had warned his mother: "If something isn’t done about Pa’s security, I know I’ll soon have to come back for his funeral."
Article Summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has revealed what went through her mind when she decided against becoming prime minister. In her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recalls how she eventually listened to her "inner voice" and decided to turn down the top post. She also explains why she chose Manmohan Singh to become prime minister, describing him as a leader of "unquestionable" integrity.

Article Title: 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Tuesday criticised Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi over her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, with party spokesperson CR Kesavan accusing her of attempting to "whitewash" the "historical wrongs" of the Nehru-Gandhi family and the Congress.In a series of post on X, Kesavan said the book should have been titled 'Whitewashing' instead of 'Belonging', alleging that its purpose was to sugarcoat the historical wrongs committed by the Nehru-Gandhi family and camouflage the Congress party's "cardinal sins".Referring to Sonia Gandhi's account of crying over the demolition of the Babri Masjid, Kesavan questioned whether she had also expressed grief over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the killing of thousands of people during the violence. "Did Sonia Gandhi even shed one tear for when the gurdwaras were attacked and innocent people, thousands of innocent people, were violently killed during the 1984 Sikh massacre which happened under the Congress rule," he said.Kesavan also referred to the Batla House encounter, alleging that Sonia Gandhi had wept for the accused, and questioned whether she had expressed similar grief for CRPF personnel killed in the line of duty."Did Sonia Gandhi even shed a single tear for the brave CRPF jawans who were martyred in the line of duty when protecting our nation and people?" he asked.He further questioned whether the memoir would address the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks and the Congress-led UPA government's response to them."Did Sonia Gandhi cry when innocent lives were lost during the horrendous 26/11 terror attacks which happened under the Congress rule? Will Sonia Gandhi's book answer?" Kesavan said, accusing the UPA government of failing to retaliate against the attacks.The BJP spokesperson also criticised Sonia Gandhi's account of the Emergency imposed by then prime minister Indira Gandhi in 1975. He accused her of attempting to justify and normalise the period, during which fundamental rights were suspended and press freedoms curtailed."The way in which Sonia Gandhi has tried to justify and normalise Indira Gandhi imposing the notorious Emergency which murdered our Constitution and suspended fundamental rights is indeed most shocking and appalling," he said.Also read: What made Sonia Gandhi turn down PM post after UPA’s 2004 victory? Memoir revisits moment Kesavan also referred to former external affairs minister K Natwar Singh’s 2014 autobiography, One Life Is Not Enough, questioning Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s visit to his residence ahead of its release. He asked whether her memoir would shed light on the meeting and the events surrounding the formation of the UPA government in May 2004."Will Smt. Sonia Gandhi's memoir also reveal the truth behind her sudden visit to late Shri. K. Natwar Singh’s residence before his book was to be published? Excerpts from Shri. K. Natwar Singh’s 2014 autobiography ‘One Life Is Not Enough’ clearly states how uneasy and uncomfortable the Nehru-Gandhi family was about his account of certain events in May 2004, before the UPA Government was sworn in," Kesavan posted on X.He further questioned why Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra had met Natwar Singh after eight and a half years and what Sonia Gandhi was apprehensive about him writing on the events leading to the UPA government's formation.Other NDA leaders also took aim at Sonia Gandhi over the memoir. JD(U) MP Sanjay Kumar Jha questioned her account of declining the Prime Minister's post in 2004, claiming that Samajwadi Party leader Mulayam Singh Yadav had refused to support her candidature. “This is a controversial matter as well. While managing numbers, what we know is that Mulayam Singh Yadav had refused to support her. Otherwise, there was a full attempt to become the PM,” Jha said.On her remarks about the Emergency, he said, “She was the PM of the country. Saying that a few people advised her is surprising.”BJP MP Rahul Sinha dismissed the significance of the memoir, saying, “Sonia Gandhi’s writings will not make any difference; nobody is going to read it.” He also criticised her support for Indira Gandhi despite the Emergency and the imprisonment of citizens.Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh minister Dinesh Pratap Singh claimed that then President APJ Abdul Kalam had refused to swear Sonia Gandhi in as Prime Minister because of her foreign origin. “President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam refused to swear in Sonia Gandhi due to her foreign origins. Later, this entire incident was portrayed as a resignation,” he said.Titled Belonging: A Journey of Love, the memoir traces Sonia Gandhi's childhood in post-war Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi while they were at Cambridge, and her life in India. It also recounts the assassinations of Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi.The memoir, which hit bookstores across India on Tuesday, also revisits the crucial political decision that shaped the UPA government's first term. Sonia also shared details of the discussions with senior Congress leaders and her final conversation with her son, Rahul Gandhi, before announcing her decision.In the memoir, Sonia also looks back at her first year as a bride in the Gandhi family, recalling her experiences of living with her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi.She describes Indira Gandhi's occasional outbursts of anger as among the "most alarming" aspects of that period. Recalling one incident, Sonia writes that a staff member who had repeatedly forgotten to remind her mother-in-law about an important appointment was made to stand in a corner of the room, while others hurried past, feeling embarrassed."What I found most alarming was my mother-in-law's occasional explosions of temper. They could freeze the staff into numbness," she wrote. In another instance, Sonia recalled noticing a "kurta-dhoti-clad individual standing immobile in the corner, staring at the wall".She also gave details on why she turned down PM post after UPA victory in 2004.Read more: Sonia recalls Indira's temper, early days as bride in memoir
Article Summary: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan accuses Sonia Gandhi of attempting to "whitewash" the "historical wrongs" of the Nehru-Gandhi family and the Congress. Kesavan also questioned whether she had expressed grief over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the killing of thousands of people during the violence.

Article Title: Person has no claim in grandpa's property held by dad, says SC
Article Text:
Person has no claim in grandpa's property held by dad, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Can a grandson claim a share in property inherited by his father from his grandfather? Supreme Court has ruled that a person becomes the absolute owner of his share in his father's ancestral or self-acquired property and can deal with it exclusively, including excluding his sons.Ending a 29-year legal battle, a bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and Sunita Agarwal rejected a son's plea for partition of his father's property. The son had filed the suit in 1997, claiming the property was ancestral or joint family property. The court said a son's son is not listed as a Class I heir under the Hindu Succession Act and cannot claim a share in his grandfather's property.Referring to Section 8, which lays down succession rules when a Hindu male dies intestate, the bench said a son becomes the absolute owner of property inherited from his father, while his own son has no right by birth over it.SC said Class I heirs inherit simultaneously, to the exclusion of all others. "A son's son is not mentioned as an heir under Class I of the Schedule, and, therefore, he could not get any right in the property of his grandfather," it said.It added that 1956 law did not preserve right under personal Hindu law of a grandson to claim a share in his grandfather's property during his father's lifetime. Sec 8 must be read as a self-contained provision governing devolution of property of a Hindu male dying intestate, it said.Citing SC judgements, the bench rejected the argument that a son inheriting property under Section 8 holds it as karta of his undivided family. Such an interpretation would create two classes among Class I heirs, treating property as joint family property for male heirs but not female heirs, it said. The express wording of Sec 8 must prevail.Upholding HC's order, the bench said a grandson cannot seek partition of property held by his father. The high court had ruled that when a son or daughter receives property through partition, whether ancestral or self-acquired, they become absolute owners of their shares and can deal with them exclusively, including excluding their sons.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rejects son's plea for partition of his father's property. The son had filed the suit in 1997, claiming the property was ancestral or joint family property. Court said a son's son is not listed as a Class I heir under the Hindu Succession Act.

Article Title: For the first time, Sonia confirms battle with cancer in memoirs
Article Text:
For the first time, Sonia confirms battle with cancer in memoirs

‘I saw

Rajiv

reaching out to me, smiling at me’

NEW DELHI: Sonia Gandhi 's memoirs, released on Tuesday, officially acknowledge what was long whispered within political circles but never publicly confirmed - her battle with cancer, which occurred during the second term of UPA govt.They also set the record straight on where her two surgeries took place - first at European Institute of Oncology, near Milan in Italy, and later at Erasmus University Medical Centre in Rotterdam - and not at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, as was widely speculated.According to Sonia , while she had suffered from occasional bouts of asthma and allergies, she had no serious health troubles until 2010, when she was advised to undergo surgery for suspected breast cancer. She chose not to get operated on in India as she wanted to avoid a media frenzy.After much discussion with her doctors, Sonia Gandhi opted to get operated on by Dr Veronesi, a celebrated surgeon who was the founder and head of the European Institute.In her book, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, Sonia writes, “On the day of the surgery, as I was wheeled into the operation theatre, Rahul and Priyanka held my hand and kissed me on the forehead, assuring me that all would be well.Afterwards, still groggy from the anaesthesia, I saw Dr Veronesi with them by my bedside. How relieved I felt to hear him announce, ‘Non c’è niente da preoccuparsi, tutto è andato bene e non ci sono residui. (No need to worry, everything has gone well and there are no residues).’ He had removed two tumours, including a non-suspicious one to be on the safe side, and conducted an intra-operative radiation to spare me five weeks of radiotherapy. ”However, a year later, routine follow-up tests detected a growth in the pancreas. This time Sonia was sent to Erasmus, to be treated by a well-known pancreatic surgeon, Dr Casper van Eijck. Again, Rahul and Priyanka were by her side before the surgery. When she woke up, dazed and parched, she heard them calling out, “Ma, Mama, all is well — nothing bad!” The doctor later explained that fortunately, the tumour was found in a preliminary precancerous stage, having been detected early.Sonia also mentions that in Aug 2016, she collapsed during a long roadshow in hot and humid weather in Varanasi and broke her shoulder in the fall, forcing her to undergo another operation. While being flown to Delhi and floating in and out of consciousness, she writes, “Then I saw him again — Rajiv, reaching out to me, smiling at me reassuringly as if to say, ‘everything will be fine’; Sheila Dikshit , who was by my side throughout, told me later that she noticed me suddenly smile in the middle of the tension-racked flight — I’m sure it must have been that moment.”Apart from these episodes, there have been no other major health scares — though, like most residents of Delhi, the toxic winter air does bother her.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoirs acknowledge what was long whispered within political circles but never publicly confirmed - her battle with cancer. They also set the record straight on where her two surgeries took place - first at European Institute of Oncology, near Milan in Italy, and later at Erasmus University Medical Centre in Rotterdam.

Article Title: 80% of Delhi's pollution Monday due to crackers
Article Text:
80% of Delhi's pollution Monday due to crackers

Vehicular emissions third biggest source of pollution day after Diwali

NEW DELHI: Firecracker emissions accounted for more than 80% of Delhi's pollution load on Monday, a day after Diwali , according to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's models, highlighting the sharp impact of fireworks on the capital's air quality. The contribution came even as the city was already battling high pollution levels from multiple sources.The situation, however, showed some improvement on Tuesday, with the AQI at 299 at 4pm, bringing it into the 'poor' category from 'very poor' a day earlier. However, it deteriorated to very poor by 6pm with an AQI of 302.Toxins from Diwali firecrackers lingered on Tuesday as well, with IITM showing 29.9% of pollution contribution due to firecrackers between 1am and 9am, while secondary organic compounds - formed due to chemical reactions of emitted particles in air - were the secondary source at 17.5% of net pollution on Tuesday. IMD attributed cleaner air to favourable wind, which helped disperse pollutants accumulated over the city and barred intrusion of stubble smoke from neighbouring states.The easing came despite a significant number of farm fires being reported in neighbouring Punjab. An assessment of the decision support system for air quality management indicated that stubble burning was not a major contributor to Delhi’s pollution load on Monday. This suggests that the immediate post-Diwali pollution spike was driven primarily by local fireworks rather than a major influx of crop-residue smoke.The high contribution from firecrackers followed a sharp deterioration in air quality during the festival. Delhi’s average AQI was 376 on Diwali, Nov 8, the highest recorded for the festival in five years. It remained in the ‘very poor’ category on Monday, with the city waking up to a thick layer of smog and several monitoring stations reporting severe air quality.IITM’s model estimates the contribution of different sources to the city’s particulate pollution a day after Diwali on Nov 9, including secondary organic compounds, at 5.8%, the second dominant source, and vehicular pollution at 4.4%, the third biggest source. However, the city’s air quality will depend on how effectively winds disperse the remaining pollutants and on emissions from routine sources.
Article Summary: Firecracker emissions accounted for more than 80% of Delhi's pollution load on Monday, a day after Diwali. The contribution came even as the city was already battling high pollution levels from multiple sources. The situation, however, showed some improvement on Tuesday, with the AQI at 299 at 4pm.

Article Title: Clinton's 'old habit', 'arrogant' Sarkozy & 'real star' Diana: Sonia's candid accounts of world leaders
Article Text:
Sonia recounts moments with world leaders in her memoir

Sarkozy's love life and an amused Sonia

Sonia's memories of Princess Diana

'I am feeling like a crow': An awkward note at the hairdresser's

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi recalls in her memoir how then-US president Bill Clinton, during his 2000 India visit, would occasionally be seen "surreptitiously sizing up the more striking women" at a reception hosted in his honour. The Monica Lewinsky scandal may have faded from the headlines by then, but, as Sonia writes, "old habits die hard".The anecdote is among several candid recollections of Sonia's interactions with global leaders and prominent personalities, including former French president Nicolas Sarkozy and the late Princess Diana, in her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey Of Love.Recalling Clinton's 2000 visit, Sonia writes about meeting the then US president at the Sheraton hotel, where he was staying with his daughter Chelsea and his delegation. She had called on him along with then-foreign minister."Friendly, informal, and exuding confidence, he appeared more keen to give us his own views and predictions about Kashmir- 'a nuclear flashpoint', in his words, 'one of the most dangerous places on earth'--than to pay attention to our point of view," she writes.Sonia also recounts a reception hosted by then-prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee in Clinton's honour, where she noticed the former US president occasionally looking at women in attendance."The Monica Lewinsky scandal had subsided a little by then, but old habits die hard; at the reception held by Prime Minister Vajpayee in his honour, I noticed him every now and then surreptitiously sizing up the more striking women present," she writes.Sonia also shares an interesting account of Nicolas Sarkozy's 2008 visit to India, when the French president travelled without his then partner, Carla Bruni."It was said that he (Sarkozy) had been advised not to bring her (Bruni) because they were unmarried which would have been awkward at official functions," she writes.At a banquet, the wife of then vice-president Mohammad Ansari, seated next to Sarkozy, began asking him about his relationship with Bruni, including whether he planned to marry her and whether a date had been fixed."President Sarkozy seemed unperturbed by the cross-examination, even eager to share details of his love life, answering all her questions while continuously messaging his Carla on his phone," Sonia recalls.The couple made a joint appearance in India on a subsequent visit, attending a private dinner hosted by then prime minister Manmohan Singh and his wife.By then, Sarkozy and Bruni had married. Sonia remembers the French president as being visibly besotted with his wife, who had been a popular singer and songwriter in Europe as well as a top model."All eyes were on her as she glided into the room in an elegant long gown, graceful and slim, demure and blue-eyed," she writes.However, Sonia's impression of the evening was not limited to Bruni's appearance. She also recalls Sarkozy holding forth on India's responsibilities while speaking to Manmohan Singh."He was obviously besotted with his tall and beautiful wife of Italian and French descent, who had been a popular singer and songwriter in Europe, as well as a top model. All eyes were on her as she glided into the room in an elegant long gown, graceful and slim, demure and blue-eyed," she writes."She spoke cordially but infrequently--while her husband held forth, expounding his views to our prime minister on what India should do in what I felt was a rather arrogant manner, unmindful of the fact that he was talking to someone more senior, more experienced and more knowledgeable," she adds.Among the most personal recollections in the memoir are Sonia's encounters with the British royal family, particularly Princess Diana.She writes that members of the British royal family had shared a friendship with the Nehru-Gandhi family over generations, while Rajiv Gandhi had got along well with Prince Charles."The real star of that family had of course been Princess Diana: Tall and slim, with large blue eyes, an enchanting smile, and a magnetic personality. I can never forget how ravishing she was as a bride when Rajiv and I attended their wedding in 1981. But when they came to India in 1992, it was evident that things were not going well in the marriage," Sonia writes.She recalls an informal meeting with the royal couple during their 1992 India visit, on the same day Diana famously posed alone on a bench in front of the Taj Mahal, later popularly known as the 'love bench'."On the very day she famously posed alone on what I call the 'love bench' in front of the Taj Mahal, they had come over for a late tea. Prince Charles was forthcoming and amusing, but she appeared morose, though looking wonderful in a striking red and purple two-piece suit. We chatted about what she had seen and liked on her visit," she writes.Sonia's mother, who was visiting at the time, was keen to meet the princess. Her daughter Priyanka was equally eager to introduce her 'Nonna' (grandmother) to Diana.When Diana wondered why Sonia's mother was so quiet, Priyanka immediately explained that she had been told not to speak because she only knew Italian."Diana burst out laughing and turned immediately to my mother, holding out her hand, "Piacere, comne stai?" ("Pleased to meet you, how are you?"), trying to pronounce the words in the correct Italian accent, though using the informal form of address, but with such warmth and charm that we all melted," Sonia recalls.The meeting ended on another warm note. As the royal couple were leaving, Diana stopped midway, turned around and waved to Sonia's mother."After tea and more chat, we were seeing them off to their car when she stopped halfway, turned back to wave to my mother, and called out, 'Ciao. Nonna!' After I presented the royal couple with my book Rajiv, she wrote to me, telling me how much she had admired my husband," Sonia writes.Sonia also recounts a later meeting with Diana in London, when she was invited for tea with the royal couple. She remembers arriving in a black suit with a white collar and joking, "I am feeling like a crow!"On another occasion, she unexpectedly came across Diana at a hairdresser's. Recognising the princess sitting next to her, Sonia decided to pass her a discreet note."I scribbled a word and passed it on to her, and the next second realised that instead of 'Hi', I had written 'Hye'. How I wished I could have snatched back the note! But it was too late; she had already put it into her handbag," she recalls.The two exchanged a few words in hushed tones, careful not to attract attention. It was the last time Sonia met Diana.Reflecting on the public scrutiny surrounding the late princess, Sonia says Diana faced considerable criticism during her lifetime, with many questioning why she appeared unhappy despite her privileged position."There was a lot of criticism of her at that time: She was spoilt and complaining; she had everything; why was she behaving as if she had been wronged? I must say I felt for her throughout, and still do," Sonia writes.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey Of Love, is out now. She recalls her interactions with world leaders, including Bill Clinton and Princess Diana. She also recalls Nicolas Sarkozy's 2008 visit to India without his then partner, Carla Bruni.

SRINAGAR: Kargil shut down Tuesday and political groups in Leh threatened an agitation after Ladakh announced Dec 4 elections to its eight autonomous hill development councils, rejecting demands to avoid holding the polls during the harsh winter months.The protests came despite chief secretary Ashish Kundra describing the elections as a “watershed moment” and a turning point for democracy in the Union territory. Article Title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: From Parliament attack to anti-terror bill passage, ex-Cong chief recalls conversations with Vajpayee
Article Text:
Parliament attack

How Sonia Gandhi's views about Vajpayee changed

When Sonia Gandhi felt her criticism of Vajpayee had gone 'too far'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: In her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," released in India on Tuesday, senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has recalled several conversations with former Prime Minister and late BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee Most of the anecdotes recounted by Sonia Gandhi date back to 1999-2004, when Vajpayee was Prime Minister and she was the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi recalled being "terrified" and calling PM Vajpayee to enquire about his safety after explosions and gunshots rang out during the terrorist attack on Parliament on December 13, 2001.According to the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson, he assured her that he was safe at home and later told many of his colleagues “appreciatively that I had been the first to call him.”The former Congress president, who was leading the grand old party at the time, also recalled being "afraid" to “stand up and confront” leaders of the ruling BJP-led coalition, who had long viewed her as “the foreign-born daughter-in-law of the Nehru-Gandhi family” — a reference to her country of birth, Italy.Nearly four months after her December 2001 conversation with Vajpayee, Sonia Gandhi’s perception of the-then Prime Minister changed when the two leaders came face to face over the Prevention of Terrorism Ordinance (POTO).In March 2002, the Vajpayee government convened a special joint sitting of Parliament to pass POTO into law after the legislation was defeated in the Rajya Sabha.Sonia Gandhi drew a contrast between the BJP’s opposition to the legislation when the Congress was in office and the saffron party's stance when it was in government.“It was a measure the BJP's heavyweights had vigorously opposed as anti-democratic in 1985 when it had been brought into existence by our government to counter the Punjab insurgency,” she writes.The Congress, in opposition at the time, argued that the ordinance “had proved ineffective in dealing with terrorism, while giving the police wide-ranging powers that could be misused against our citizens."She recounted that the joint sitting was held in the Central Hall of the old Parliament building, which was replaced by the new Parliament complex inaugurated in May 2023. She described the hall as “a much larger and more intimidating space”, with "imposing" portraits of leaders of the freedom struggle adorning its walls.“Prime Minister Vajpayee had chosen not to speak on this vitally important issue. Towards the end of the session, when the Speaker called out my name, I walked to the podium, full of trepidation. I had just finished reading out my speech, when the Speaker surprised everyone by calling out the name of the Prime Minister.”Vajpayee then appeared in the Central Hall, “his expression sullen”, and began speaking. According to Sonia Gandhi, his speech focused not on the legislation but on questioning her “inexperience and lack of skill in oratory”.“He had taken offence at my asking whether he would ‘uphold the prestige of his high office’ or be ‘submissive and weak in his leadership’. So that was his purpose in returning to the House! How dare I question his leadership abilities, who was I to place him in the dock?“He launched into a full-blown attack on my inexperience and my lack of skill in oratory, berating me so that our MPs rose to their feet in protest. The other side did the same, and soon all were not only vociferously shouting one another down but almost coming to blows. I cannot deny I felt wounded,” Gandhi writes in the book.The joint sitting ended with the passage of the bill, which was later repealed by the Congress-led UPA government in 2004.A few months later, when Sonia Gandhi saw that Vajpayee had “aged visibly and was looking far from well”, she felt she had “gone a bit too far” in her criticism of him.“...he was a veteran leader, and though we belonged to opposing ideologies, he was the prime minister, and I should have been more moderate in criticising him,” she writes.The 526-page memoir, published by HarperCollins India, traces Sonia Gandhi’s life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi family to the assassination of her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and her eventual entry into politics.
Article Summary: In her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has recalled several conversations with former Prime Minister and late BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Most of the anecdotes recounted by Sonia Gandhi date back to 1999-2004, when Vaj payee was PM and she was leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha.

Article Title: 'No, I won't let our baby be thrown into river': Sonia recalls loss of first child before Rahul
Article Text:
Before Rahul, Sonia and Rajiv lost first child; memoir reveals details (Picture from X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In September 1968, the Gandhi household was filled with joy when Sonia Gandhi announced her pregnancy. Even the usually stern Indira Gandhi broke into a rare display of affection, embracing her daughter-in-law Sonia Gandhi and exclaiming, “One big baby having another baby!”But the happiness was short-lived.Sonia gave birth to a premature baby boy on January 18, 1969, two months before her due date. Initially overjoyed, the family was soon devastated by the newborn’s death.In her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recounts the deeply personal tragedy for the first time. She writes that the baby was buried by her husband Rajiv Gandhi and brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi at Feroze Gandhi’s farmhouse in Mehrauli.“I heard the baby's first cry as he was placed in the incubator. Later Rajiv took me to see him, a tiny, perfectly formed boy, with thick, black hair and long, slim fingers. We gazed at him together, Rajiv's arm around my shoulder. We fell in love with him immediately,” she writes.Doctors had warned Rajiv that the baby’s chances of survival were uncertain. At 6:30 am, he was informed that the newborn had died.“With Amie Aunty beside him, he broke it gently to me when at 6:30 in the morning the end came.‘No it was not possible! Why, why,’ I kept asking. Both of us were shocked and heartbroken, we held each other tight. I cried my heart out, and Rajiv, in spite of his ‘stiff upper lip’ upbringing, also wept copiously,” she recalls.Indira, who was away on a tour, cut short her visit and rushed to the hospital.“She embraced us, her eyes red and swollen, and sat with us for a long time. She wanted to remain with us, she said, but had to complete her tour engagement. She left early the next morning, full of sorrow: She, too, had so looked forward to the happy event.”The family then faced the difficult question of the newborn’s last rites. Sonia writes that, according to Hindu tradition, a newborn could not be cremated and was traditionally released into a river.However, the thought brought back a disturbing memory of seeing a swollen male body trapped near the Okhla barrage, with scavenging dogs trying to pull it out.“‘No,’ I whispered. ‘No matter what, I'm not going to allow our baby to be thrown into the river.’...’No, I couldn't do that to my baby, no matter how sacred the river was,’ I said, breaking into sobs. How could I consent to do something that seemed to me so alien and heartless to my tiny child, already deprived of his chance to live?”The family eventually decided to bury the child at Feroze Gandhi’s farmhouse in Mehrauli.“It was a painful and agonising option, but there was no other way. Rajiv came back to the hospital and told me that he and Sanjay had buried the little one deep under a beautiful pink bougainvillea bush, then in full bloom on the left side along the inner boundary wall," she recounts.“For a long time we'd pause and place a flower over the spot each time we went there. It didn't assuage our pain, but we had to accept the inevitable,” she writes.Sonia also recalls how Indira had closely monitored her pregnancy, advising her on diet, walks and exercise. She writes that she had no major discomfort, apart from missing Italian food and developing a craving for jamun, phalsa and Fanta, sometimes drinking twelve glasses a day.The loss left her depressed and struggling with feelings of inadequacy and guilt. The pain was compounded by a right-wing opposition newspaper publishing an article titled, "Indira Gandhi failed in her attempt to become the grandmother of a bastard child."“The venom of those words scarred my heart. How could people be so cruel? What had I done to deserve such malice? The hurt caused by that spiteful comment added to the heartbreak of my loss and to my feeling of inadequacy,” she writes.In October 1969, Sonia told Rajiv she was pregnant again. “Thrilled but anxious”, she gave birth to their second child, Rahul Gandhi , on June 19, 1970.
Article Summary: Sonia gave birth to a premature baby boy on January 18, 1969, two months before her due date. In her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recounts the deeply personal tragedy for the first time. She writes that the baby was buried by her husband Rajiv Gandhi and brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi.

Article Title: 'No real contact with him': Sonia Gandhi recalls face-to-face meetings with PM Modi in memoir
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi also criticised PM Modi's language in Parliament, alleging that he sometimes uses the same coarse language he employs at public rallies.

‘We come from different ideological worlds’

Sonia Gandhi on PM Modi's rise within the RSS

‘Coarse language’ and attacks on opposition in Parliament

‘Congress-free India’: Sonia on BJP's opposition to Congress

Sonia Gandhi recalls 2002 Gujarat riots

Sonia Gandhi on her understanding of Hinduism and faith

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, in her memoir, has said that she has had "practically no real contact" with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, despite his more than 12 years in office. She writes that PM Modi tends to look away and avoid eye contact when they come face-to-face.In her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi said their interactions were largely limited to formal greetings at official gatherings and brief exchanges about her health.Describing their occasional encounters, Sonia said they usually meet at semi-official gatherings, such as the meetings of major political party leaders in the Speaker's chamber at the end of Parliament sessions."It's a very small room, and usually many people are present, but when he comes face-to-face with me, we greet each other with a formal namaste. This is different from the past, when leaders across party divides would treat one another with cordiality. He tends to look away, avoiding eye contact," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi recalled that PM Modi had occasionally enquired about her health after she returned from a hospital stay.He asked, "Theek hain aap?" to which she would reply, "Jee, ab main theek hoon, shukriya.""Apart from such brief exchanges, we have never really conversed, though we've exchanged formal birthday and New Year greetings over the years," she added.Sonia Gandhi said her limited interaction with PM Modi was also set against a wider ideological divide between the two leaders. She described their political rivalry as a contest between contrasting visions of India, rather than a personal feud."We come from different ideological worlds; his idea of this country is vastly different from mine," she wrote.Explaining the difference, Sonia said, "All I learnt about India was assimilated from the members of my family, their lives of service, and their faith in a nation that encompassed a host of races and cultures, languages and faiths, based on principles of liberty and equality for all."On the contrary, she said PM Modi's vision of India was shaped by the RSS and his upbringing."Narendra Modi’s idea of India was constructed by the ideologues of the RSS and the experience of his own growing up. It affirmed a fundamentalism in which his faith and culture superseded all others. In that India, hierarchy, order, and control are central."Sonia said she stood for an India based on inclusiveness, secularism and social justice."He was fighting for his vision of India, and I for mine: an India against hegemony, an India that stands for inclusiveness, secularism, and social justice. It wasn't personal," she wrote.Sonia acknowledged that PM Modi had worked his way up within the RSS from an underprivileged background. However, she questioned the way his humble origins had been portrayed by his public relations team."Modi's origins may not have been as humble as his PR team has made out in marketing his image, but he had certainly worked his way to power within the RSS from an underprivileged world," she wrote.She also said PM Modi's political journey had been very different from hers. However, she found herself able to understand some of his discomfort with the ruling elite.Recalling her own experiences in Delhi's political circles, Sonia Gandhi said she often felt out of place during discussions in privileged drawing rooms. The views expressed there, she said, were far removed from the realities of ordinary Indians.She added that the suffering and struggle for survival she had witnessed in her constituency and during her travels across the country were unimaginable to this privileged group.Sonia Gandhi also criticised PM Modi's language in Parliament, alleging that he sometimes uses the same coarse language he employs at public rallies."When speaking in Parliament, he at times uses the same coarse language he employs in addressing a public rally. Much of the time he derides the opposition in what can only be termed a tirade," she wrote.She also accused the BJP of repeatedly targeting India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, for establishing the country's democratic and secular foundations."Jawaharlal Nehru, our first prime minister, is a particular target of his party's hostility, for having set our country on a democratic and secular course," Sonia wrote.She further alleged that Sangh Parivar websites were filled with malicious abuse and falsehoods against Nehru.Sonia Gandhi described the BJP's stated goal of a "Congress-free India" as an attempt to eliminate not just the party but also its policies and ideology.She said she believed the hostility towards Congress stemmed from the prime minister's conditioning by the RSS."I tend to believe that this antipathy stems from the conditioning of the prime minister by the RSS. It has inculcated in its cadre a commitment to an exclusionary, hardened version of Hinduism that has been crafted into a political agenda," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi also revisited the 2002 Gujarat riots, which took place when PM Modi was the state's chief minister.Recalling the violence that followed the Godhra train tragedy, she said the Sabarmati Express was returning to Ahmedabad from Ayodhya with Hindu kar sevaks when four coaches caught fire. Fifty-nine pilgrims were killed. She noted that the cause of the fire remained disputed, while the communal violence that followed spread to several parts of Gujarat and claimed predominantly Muslim victims."When I was leader of the opposition in Parliament, I met the victims of many tragedies, and each time I was haunted by the misery I had witnessed," she wrote.She recalled watching television reports of the violence and trying to reach Congress colleagues in Gujarat who were seeking help."We watched the live reports in horror, and tried to get help to our colleagues in Gujarat who were calling us in desperation, but the administration failed to respond," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi said the riots were reported to have been fuelled by a fanatical fringe of the BJP and RSS, including the Bajrang Dal. PM Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat at the time.Sonia also contrasted the RSS's political interpretation of Hinduism with the inclusive understanding of faith she said she had learnt from her mother-in-law.She described this understanding as one that embraced different beliefs and paths, without being tied to a single deity, dogma, prophet or scripture."What I learnt from my mother-in-law is the faith that's been practised for centuries in India by vast numbers of our people -- from stalwarts of the freedom struggle to the poorest in our villages. It embraces diverse beliefs and different paths, adheres to no single deity, dogma, prophet, or scripture, and has included traditions of dissent," she wrote.She added that she had been educated in the principles of ahimsa and dharma as interpreted by Mahatma Gandhi. She also acknowledged the oppression and inequality associated with India's caste system, while pointing out that reformers had used ideas within Hinduism to challenge caste discrimination.
Article Summary: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi has said she has had "practically no real contact" with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She writes that PM Modi tends to look away and avoid eye contact when they come face-to-face. She also criticised PM Modi's language in Parliament, alleging that he sometimes uses the same coarse language he employs at public rallies.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael Maye, have found a personal way to celebrate a year filled with major milestones. The couple’s first holiday card since getting married features a photograph from their anniversary trip to Cabo, offering a glimpse into their life away from the NFL. Ann Michael, 23, shared the card exclusively with PEOPLE on November 10 through her partnership with Minted. Beyond the Christmas greeting, the card carries memories of their travels, their first year of marriage and the quieter moments they have managed to enjoy together.The photograph on the front of the card takes the couple back to their first wedding anniversary trip to Cabo during the NFL offseason. Ann Michael wears a brown sundress with blue polka dots, while Drake keeps his look relaxed in a white collared shirt, navy pants and sunglasses. The design, called “Apres Ski” by Wildfield Paper Co., carries a simple “Merry Christmas” message and the Maye family signature.For Ann Michael, the photograph was more than a choice that looked good on a Christmas card. It reminded her of a period when the couple could put their busy schedules aside and enjoy time together.“We chose a photo from our first anniversary trip to Cabo during the offseason. It’s been such an exciting and eventful year for us, and this photo brings back a really happy memory of Drake and me getting to slow down, spend time together, and just soak it all in,” she tells PEOPLE.The couple's relationship has already included several important milestones. Childhood sweethearts, Drake and Ann Michael got engaged in January 2025 and married in June that year. Drake's journey with the New England Patriots also brought plenty of attention, including the team's run to Super Bowl 2026 in February.Amid those developments, Ann Michael said finding time for each other has become particularly valuable.“With everything going on in our lives, those quieter moments together are really special, and I love that we get to share one of them with our friends and family this holiday season,” she says.The Mayes began sending holiday cards only after their wedding, but the tradition has quickly become something Ann Michael looks forward to every year. She sees the cards as a way to preserve memories rather than simply send seasonal greetings.“We started sending holiday cards after we got married, and it’s quickly become a tradition I absolutely love!” Ann Michael shares. “There’s something so special about sending a personal note to friends and family, especially during the holidays.”She also wanted the cards to become a record of their changing lives. “I love the idea of looking back years from now and seeing how our lives have changed through our holiday cards,” she continues, adding, “It’s a sweet way to capture a little snapshot of each year.”There is more to the card than the Cabo photograph. Ann Michael included highlights from the couple's travels on the back, with trips to the Masters and Japan among the memories featured.“One detail you might not notice at first glance is that we included a few highlights from our travels on the back of the card, including trips to the Masters and Japan!” she shares. “We’ve made so many wonderful memories together this year, and I loved being able to share a few more of those moments with our friends and family.”She calls the extra touch “almost like a little year-in-review!”Ann Michael wanted the overall design to feel classic rather than follow a passing trend. Minted's independent artist designs and concierge service helped her find a style that matched the photograph and the couple's taste. She also has plans to bring some football spirit into their Christmas celebrations, even though the holiday card itself does not feature the Patriots.“I am planning a Patriots-themed red and blue Christmas tree this holiday season!” she shares.Her hope is that the card makes friends and family smile. After a year of marriage, travel and major football moments, the Mayes have chosen to preserve something less public: the memories they made together.

The couple's first holiday card since getting married features a photograph from their anniversary trip to Cabo. Ann Michael included highlights from the couple's travels on the back, with trips to the Masters and Japan among the memories featured.

Article Title: Aryna Sabalenka controversy: beIN SPORTS apologises after commentator's shocking on-air remark goes viral
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka (Image via Getty Images)

Aryna Sabalenka faces appearance controversy as beIN SPORTS issues apology

Aryna Sabalenka defeats Karolina Muchova despite difficult WTA Finals start

Aryna Sabalenka found herself at the centre of an uncomfortable controversy at the WTA Finals, but this time, the attention had little to do with her tennis. A comment about the Belarusian star's appearance was accidentally picked up during a live broadcast, leaving viewers stunned. The clip quickly circulated online, prompting criticism of the broadcaster. As the backlash grew, beIN SPORTS France issued a public apology, with a senior executive condemning the remark and distancing the network from the incident.The incident unfolded during Sabalenka's player introduction at the WTA Finals. As the camera focused on the World No. 2, an off-air conversation became audible to viewers watching the coverage.A commentator could be heard saying, “Look, look… she looks horrible.”The remark immediately attracted criticism after a clip surfaced on the tennis account Tiempo De Tenis. Another account, L’Arene, shared the footage and directly tagged beIN SPORTS France, demanding a response over the comment.Viewers questioned why a professional athlete's appearance had become a subject of discussion during an important tournament broadcast.The controversy soon reached the broadcaster's management.Florent Houzot, beIN SPORTS France's Director of Broadcast Operations, Programming, and Editorial, addressed the situation publicly. He expressed regret and strongly criticised the comments made during the coverage.“I regret and strongly condemn the remarks made live on air this evening during the WTA Finals broadcast,” Houzot said.He also stressed that the comments did not reflect the broadcaster's values and reaffirmed its commitment to respecting athletes and everyone involved in sports coverage.However, the identity of the commentator and any possible disciplinary action remain unconfirmed.The situation has drawn comparisons with another tennis broadcasting controversy from November 2024. Tennis Channel commentator Jon Wertheim faced criticism after making remarks about Barbora Krejcikova's forehead during WTA Finals coverage in Riyadh.Wertheim later apologised, while Tennis Channel removed him from its broadcasts indefinitely. The network also issued an apology to Krejcikova.There is no confirmation that beIN SPORTS will take similar action in Sabalenka's case.Away from the controversy, Sabalenka had business to handle on court. The two-time Grand Slam champion opened her WTA Finals campaign with a 7-6(2), 7-5 victory over Karolina Muchova.It was far from an easy evening. Muchova broke Sabalenka early and even served for the opening set. However, the Belarusian recovered and dominated the tiebreak.The second set brought another challenge, with both players exchanging breaks before Sabalenka finally secured the victory.Her serve also caused problems. She recorded seven double faults and four aces, landing only 59% of her first serves.Explaining the difficult conditions, Sabalenka said, “It was a bit tricky with the sun [and] with the shade. Sometimes I had to adjust my toss, sometimes I had to serve blind, but it’s all part of the game,” Sabalenka said.The win gave her a positive start in her sixth consecutive WTA Finals appearance. Having finished runner-up in 2022 and 2025, Sabalenka remains determined to capture her first title at the season-ending tournament.
Article Summary: Aryna Sabalenka beat Karolina Muchova 7-6(2), 7-5 at the WTA Finals. A comment about the Belarusian star's appearance was accidentally picked up during a live broadcast, leaving viewers stunned. The clip quickly circulated online, prompting criticism of the broadcaster. beIN SPORTS France issued a public apology.

Article Title: “That could use my help”: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus makes big move to rescue Brandon Aiyuk’s NFL career as San Francisco 49ers weigh his future
Article Text:
Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus makes big move to rescue Brandon Aiyuk’s NFL career

Drew Rosenhaus prepares to find Brandon Aiyuk a new NFL team

Tyreek Hill's agent hints at Brandon Aiyuk's potential landing spot amid $13 million dispute

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brandon Aiyuk has a way back into the NFL, but it may not come with the San Francisco 49ers. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, expects the wide receiver to play this season and is already preparing for the possibility of finding him on another team.Rosenhaus, who also represents former Miami Dolphins star Tyreek Hill, has helped Aiyuk reconnect with San Francisco and complete the steps needed for reinstatement. However, head coach Kyle Shanahan's latest comments suggest the 49ers have little interest in bringing the receiver back.Rosenhaus has already made one important move. After taking over Aiyuk's representation, he arranged a meeting between the receiver and the 49ers on November 6. The meeting took place at the team's business offices in Santa Clara, where Aiyuk completed a physical and showed that he was ready to resume his career.The NFL officially reinstated Aiyuk on November 9, giving San Francisco a two-week roster exemption. That period runs until November 23, leaving the 49ers with time to decide whether to keep him, trade him or release him.Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Rosenhaus explained why he took on Aiyuk's case."I'm in the business of helping players and I felt like this was a player that could use my help. He was in a dilemma, no man's land," the agent said.Rosenhaus also spoke about his relationship with the 49ers, praising head coach Kyle Shanahan, general manager John Lynch and the organisation. He said he used those connections to bring both sides together.However, Shanahan's reaction to Aiyuk's reinstatement offered little hope of a reunion. Speaking to reporters after the NFL's decision, the 49ers coach said, "It means absolutely nothing to our team." He also described the exemption as an administrative matter.Rosenhaus understands the situation and is already preparing for a different outcome."Judging the comments from Coach Shanahan, it doesn't sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back. So when the two weeks is over, it's my job to potentially find a new team for him," he said on The Pat McAfee Show.The agent also confirmed that Aiyuk has been working out independently. He has been running routes and catching footballs, and Rosenhaus is willing to arrange a workout for interested franchises if San Francisco releases him.Rosenhaus has not named a potential destination, but he offered a clue about the kind of franchise that could sign Aiyuk. The agent believes the receiver would benefit from joining a team that already knows his game."I think that in all likelihood Brandon would probably sign with a team that knows him, somebody that has somehow been affiliated with him either in college or the 49ers," Rosenhaus said on The Pat McAfee Show on November 10.That could put franchises with connections to Aiyuk's college career at Arizona State or his time in San Francisco in the conversation. However, Rosenhaus did not confirm any team's interest.There is also a financial issue that could complicate Aiyuk's departure. The 49ers are seeking approximately $13 million in bonus money that the receiver allegedly owes the franchise. San Francisco also voided $27 million in guaranteed money for 2026 after he missed required meetings and team activities during his rehabilitation.Rosenhaus made it clear that the money dispute and Aiyuk's playing future are two separate matters."He hasn't paid anything yet. That's something that we'll work out separately and distinct from the issue of him playing," the agent said on the show.Aiyuk has not played since October 20, 2024, when he suffered ACL and MCL injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs. Before that setback, he had enjoyed the best season of his career in 2023, finishing with 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. He also earned second-team All-Pro honours.Now, Rosenhaus wants to turn that production into another NFL opportunity. With the November 23 deadline approaching, Aiyuk's next move could take him away from San Francisco. The agent believes he can get the receiver back on the field, even if the 49ers are no longer part of the plan.
Article Summary: Brandon Aiyuk was reinstated by the NFL on November 9. The San Francisco 49ers have a two-week roster exemption until November 23. The 49ers are seeking approximately $13 million in bonus money that the receiver allegedly owes the franchise. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has said that the exemption means "absolutely nothing to our team"

Article Title: Tom Brady's plea for dying mentor sparked 600 donor registrations before unexpected kidney donation saved mother of two
Article Text:
Tom Brady (Image via Reuters)

Tom Brady's emotional kidney donor appeal brings 600 responses

Peter Hughes donates kidney to save mother of two Ajisa Bethiel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2012, Tom Brady wanted to save the life of a man who had shaped his football career. But his emotional appeal for a kidney donor ended up changing another family's future in an unexpected way. The New England Patriots legend reached out to the public when his longtime mentor, Tom Martinez, desperately needed a transplant. Around 600 people responded to the appeal. Martinez never received the kidney he needed, but one man's decision to donate eventually gave a mother of two a second chance at life. It became one of the most remarkable stories connected to Brady's life away from football.Martinez was more than a football coach to Tom Brady. He had worked with the quarterback since his teenage years and played an important role in developing his throwing technique. Their relationship continued long after Brady entered the NFL.However, Martinez faced a serious health crisis when his kidneys began failing. He needed a transplant, and finding a suitable donor became increasingly urgent.Brady decided to use his public profile to help. He appealed to people to register as potential kidney donors through MatchingDonors.com, hoping someone could help the man who had guided him throughout his career.The response was remarkable. Around 600 people registered after Brady's appeal attracted widespread attention.Sadly, Martinez died in February 2012 before receiving a transplant. His death was a devastating loss for Brady, who had hoped to repay his mentor in some way.Yet the appeal had already set something unexpected in motion.Among the people who responded to Brady's appeal was Peter Hughes, a resident of Sterling, Massachusetts. Although Martinez could not receive his donation, Hughes decided that he still wanted to help someone in need.His decision eventually brought him to Ajisa Bethiel, a mother of two from Lexington, Massachusetts.Bethiel had escaped war-torn Bosnia in 1994 and later faced serious kidney problems. Finding a suitable donor was difficult, and her future remained uncertain while she waited for a transplant.Hughes eventually donated one of his kidneys to Bethiel at Massachusetts General Hospital in May 2012.The transplant gave Bethiel a new opportunity to live a healthier life and spend more time with her children.Brady's original intention had been to help his beloved coach. Although that effort could not save Martinez, the public appeal encouraged hundreds of people to consider organ donation. One man's decision ultimately helped save another person's life.It was an extraordinary reminder that a single act of kindness can reach far beyond its original purpose. Brady never set out to change Bethiel's life, but his determination to help his mentor helped create an opportunity that she desperately needed.
Article Summary: Tom Brady appealed to the public for a kidney donor for his mentor, Tom Martinez. Around 600 people responded to the appeal. Martinez never received the kidney he needed, but one man's decision to donate eventually gave a mother of two a second chance at life.

Article Title: All about Patrick Mahomes' three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden, as he and Brittany prepare to welcome baby No. 4
Article Text:
Patrick and Brittany Mahomes with their 3 kids (Instagram)

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are preparing to welcome their fourth child

Sterling Skye Mahomes was their first child

Patrick “Bronze” Mahomes III joined the family in 2022

Golden Raye Mahomes completed their family of five

Patrick Mahomes wants his children to choose their own path
