Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes , are preparing to welcome their fourth child, adding another member to a family that has grown alongside the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback's remarkable NFL career. The couple already share three children: Sterling Skye, Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III and Golden Raye. From Sterling's first appearance on the football field to Bronze and Golden joining their parents at major family celebrations, each child has had a special place in their lives. Their growing family also reflects Patrick's approach to fatherhood, which has always centered on letting his children find their own interests.The Mahomes family is getting ready for another major change. Patrick and Brittany have already experienced the demands and happiness of raising three young children, and baby No. 4 will make their household even bigger.The couple's journey into parenthood began in 2021, shortly after Patrick proposed to Brittany at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl ring ceremony on September 1, 2020. Later that month, they announced that they were expecting their first child.Brittany shared the pregnancy news with a photograph of the couple holding a sonogram, writing, “Just taking a small detour to the wedding😬❤️.”They married on March 12, 2022, in a ceremony that included their daughter Sterling as the flower girl. Patrick had previously told PEOPLE that he hoped his daughter would be part of the wedding. Brittany later confirmed that Sterling had indeed taken on the role, making the occasion even more special for the family.Sterling Skye Mahomes was born on February 20, 2021, in Kansas City, Missouri. Patrick and Brittany announced her arrival with a photograph of their newborn holding her father's finger. Their announcement also revealed her birth details: 6 pounds and 11 ounces.The couple initially decided against sharing Sterling's face publicly. Brittany explained that they wanted to wait until they felt comfortable doing so. Sterling eventually made her Instagram debut in June 2021, four months after her birth.She soon became a familiar face among Chiefs fans. Sterling appeared alongside her father in an Oakley commercial, giving Patrick another reason to celebrate his daughter's growing personality.“We got a special day. We got Ster-Ster’s first commercial,” Patrick said at the time. “She’s going to be the real star of the family.”Sterling has also developed a noticeable connection with her father's football career. During the 2022 season, she and Brittany wore matching Chiefs-inspired outfits, including red pants and black shirts with the Mahomes name.Her game-day wardrobe became even more personal in 2024. Sterling wore a custom denim outfit featuring patches referencing Patrick, including his jersey number and the word “daddy.”Brittany spoke about her daughter's excitement around game days in January 2024. “She truly enjoys going down to the field and getting to see him before the game,” she told PEOPLE. “I think it’s a very special moment wherever I get to bring them to the game and they get to watch their dad play football.”The Mahomes family welcomed its first son on November 28, 2022. Patrick and Brittany announced his arrival through Instagram, introducing him as Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III.The announcement featured a photograph of the newborn's feet resting on a fleece blanket bearing the Mahomes name. A custom diamond chain with Bronze's name was also placed beside him.His arrival brought a new dynamic to the household. Brittany had already experienced motherhood with Sterling, but managing two young children presented its own challenges.In December 2022, she offered a glimpse of those early parenting days on X, writing, “Today is my first day of chaos since having 2 kids,” before adding, “Both screaming, both not wanting to nap.”Bronze also became part of the family's Super Bowl traditions at an early age. He accompanied Brittany and Sterling to the 2023 Super Bowl in Arizona and the 2024 championship game in Las Vegas.Patrick even celebrated his son's second birthday through a footwear collaboration. Ahead of the occasion in November 2024, the quarterback unveiled the Mahomes 2 Impact FLX Bronze training shoes with Adidas.“Celebrating Bronze’s birthday with his own colorway,” Patrick wrote on Instagram.Patrick and Brittany welcomed their third child, Golden Raye Mahomes, on January 12, 2025. The couple announced her arrival through a joint Instagram post featuring a black-and-white photograph of their daughter's tiny feet held by her parents.“•Golden Raye Mahomes•1/12/25🎀✨,” the announcement read.They had revealed the pregnancy in July 2024 with a family video documenting a photoshoot. “Round three, here we come,” they wrote alongside the announcement. The couple later confirmed that they were expecting another girl.Golden's name also continued the family's distinctive naming tradition. Sterling, Bronze and Golden all draw inspiration from precious metals, giving the three siblings a shared connection through their names.Her first birthday in January 2026 brought another family celebration. Brittany shared footage from a flower-themed party featuring a bouncy castle and a ball pit.“Celebrated our Golden girl with the best crew,” she wrote.While football is central to Patrick's professional life, he has made it clear that he does not intend to push his children towards the same career.During an October 2022 appearance on Football in America, the quarterback discussed how he planned to approach his children's potential sporting interests.“I'm going to teach my son, my daughter all the fundamentals and whatever they want to learn,” the three-time Super Bowl MVP explained. “But at the same time ... I want to let it be about them ... That's what my dad did growing up, that's what my parents did. They didn't pressure me to do anything. I think that's why I'm in the position I am today.”That approach offers a glimpse into how Patrick views his responsibilities away from the NFL. He wants his children to have the freedom to explore their interests rather than inherit expectations because of their father's achievements.With Sterling, Bronze and Golden already part of the family, the arrival of their fourth child will bring another chapter to the Mahomes household. Patrick may be one of football's biggest stars, but his own words suggest that he wants his children to build identities that have little to do with his reputation on the field.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, are preparing to welcome their fourth child. The couple already share three children: Sterling Skye, Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III and Golden Raye. Their growing family reflects Patrick's approach to fatherhood, which has always centered on letting his children find their own interests.

Article Title: How P.K. Subban’s luxury lifestyle extends beyond hockey: Exploring his high-end real estate, Beverly Hills villa, interior design choices, media career and philanthropy after the NHL
Article Text:
How P.K. Subban kept his $10M promise to a children’s hospital and helped 100,000 kids

Inside NHL legend P.K. Subban’s luxury lifestyle and real estate investments

Inside P.K. Subban’s former Beverly Hills luxury home

P.K. Subban built his reputation with an energetic style of play, a standout personality and accomplishments with the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils, and he won the Norris Trophy in 2013 and became one of the most recognizable personalities in hockey, drawing attention for his play, his sense of fashion and his off-ice persona.Subban has continued to build his profile with broadcasting, public appearances and charity initiatives since retiring from professional hockey in 2022. His lifestyle also suggests a love of luxury real estate and well-thought-out interiors. Details of his current real estate portfolio remain private, but his former Beverly Hills residence with Olympian Lindsey Vonn is a documented case of the plush residential style that goes with his public persona.Subban's career in the NHL provided the platform for a lifestyle that combines professional success, travel, fashion and property interests. Across his playing years, he represented the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils, becoming known for his confidence and distinctive personality. His career achievements also helped establish his profile beyond Canadian and American hockey audiences.Real estate became one visible part of that lifestyle. Subban and former fiancée Lindsey Vonn purchased a luxury property in Beverly Hills, California, during their relationship. The home was of interest for its location, architecture and amenities, and for an insight into the residential choices of two high-profile athletes.One of the most talked-about properties associated with Subban was the Beverly Hills villa he purchased with Lindsey Vonn in April 2020 for approximately $6.75 million. The former couple later listed the property for $7.175 million following their separation and sold it for $6.9 million in 2021. The transaction attracted attention in the luxury real estate market because of the property's architecture, location and extensive amenities.The Italian-inspired residence covered approximately 5,564 square feet and featured four bedrooms and six bathrooms, and located in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, the property offered privacy, spacious living areas and views of the surrounding canyon landscape.Subban's interest in fashion has been a recognizable part of his public personality. He has often been seen in carefully chosen suits, with distinctive accessories and attention to detail. That emphasis on presentation is what provides context to the polished look of the Beverly Hills property.The villa was designed with a mix of traditional architectural features and modern finishes, and neutral interiors, expansive windows and open spaces helped create a bright atmosphere, while marble surfaces and statement features added a sense of luxury.Subban officially announced his retirement from professional hockey on September 20, 2022, ending a 13-season NHL career. He finished with 834 regular-season games, 115 goals and 352 assists, recording 467 points across spells with the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils. His achievements included the 2013 Norris Trophy as the league's top defenseman.Retirement did not mean leaving hockey behind. ESPN signed Subban to a multiyear agreement in November 2022, bringing him into its NHL coverage as an in-studio analyst and occasional in-game contributor. The role gave him an opportunity to use his experience as a former player to discuss team performances, individual players and major league developments.ESPN also said he will host “P.K.’s Places,” a series in which he visits hockey icons and sites of interest in the game’s history. Making the switch to broadcasting allowed him to remain involved with the NHL and develop a new professional identity.Subban’s broadcasting presence also plays off the personality that made him popular in his playing career. His energetic way of communicating, his sense of humor and his willingness to talk about fashion and culture have helped his work stand out against traditional game analysis.Outside of TV, he’s remained active in hockey-related events and projects, all in an effort to grow the game’s audience. As a Toronto-born player who played for Canada internationally, he also has ties to Canadian hockey communities.Philanthropy has been one of the most significant parts of Subban's life beyond professional hockey, and in September 2015, he announced a commitment to donate $10 million to the Montreal Children's Hospital through the P.K. Subban Foundation. The pledge was intended to support children and families receiving treatment at the hospitalThat dedication didn’t end when Subban left Montreal for Nashville in 2016. He remained affiliated with the hospital, visiting the young patients and continuing to support the institution. The Nashville Predators documented his visits with teammates, highlighting how the initiative was more than just a financial donation.In a 2023 publication, the Montreal Children’s Hospital Foundation said it had raised $6.3 million to date on the $10 million pledge. This allows for a documented update on the initiative instead of presuming that the entire commitment was already completedSubban also won the NHL's King Clancy Memorial Trophy in 2022 for his leadership and humanitarian work. His foundation has supported underserved youth, youth hockey, racial and social justice initiatives and COVID-19 relief efforts.His philanthropy adds another dimension to his public persona. Beyond hockey, he is interested in luxury property, fashion and broadcasting, and his dedication to the hospital is a sign of how he has given back to communities with his professional success.Life after the NHL P.K. Subban lives in several places. His previous villa in Beverly Hills showed an interest in high-end residential living, and his role at ESPN kept him in touch with the sport that made his name. But the philanthropy, especially the pledge to the Montreal Children’s Hospital, continues to define his legacy off the ice.

Article Title: Travis Kelce-backed $200 million Six Flags agrees to $11.2 million deal after customers accuse company of sneaking in extra fees
Article Text:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

$8 in cash

December 22, 2026

Six Flags, the amusement park giant associated with Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce , has agreed to an $11.2 million settlement following allegations that customers faced hidden fees while booking tickets online. The case could bring cash payments to more than 1.4 million eligible California customers. Although the lawsuit does not involve Kelce personally, his reported connection to the company adds a celebrity angle to a dispute over ticket prices and consumer rights.The settlement also raises a familiar question for families planning a day out: How much should a ticket really cost? For some customers, the answer allegedly changed just before they paid.The legal dispute began in June 2024 when Sargis Isayan filed a class-action lawsuit against Cedar Fair, L.P., which operated Knott's Berry Farm and California's Great America.According to court documents cited by PEOPLE, Isayan accused the operator of the “unlawful practice of ‘drip pricing.’ ”The complaint alleged that customers saw one ticket price while browsing, only to encounter an extra processing charge during checkout.Isayan argued that the added fee offered no real benefit. By the time customers reached the payment page, many had already spent time choosing tickets and were less likely to cancel their purchase.Cedar Fair merged with Six Flags Entertainment Corporation in July 2024, bringing the parks under the combined business.Six Flags has not admitted wrongdoing. Instead, the company agreed to resolve the dispute through an $11.2 million settlement, subject to court approval.The case highlights a wider concern about online pricing. When businesses reveal extra charges late in a transaction, customers may struggle to compare the true cost of different options.The settlement comes as Travis Kelce's reported ambassador and investor ties to Six Flags draw attention to the amusement park business. However, there is no indication that the Chiefs tight end participated in the alleged pricing practices or played any role in the lawsuit.The proposed agreement covers California customers who bought eligible non-season tickets online for Knott's Berry Farm, Knott's Soak City or California's Great America between June 28, 2020, and July 1, 2024.Customers must also have entered a California billing ZIP code and paid a processing fee.Approximately 1,405,235 people may qualify.Eligible customers who submit valid claims can receive. Those who do not file will automatically receive an $8 voucher for future purchases through Six Flags, provided they qualify under the settlement terms.The vouchers expire 36 months after issuance.Customers seeking cash must submit their claims by, through the official settlement website, http://www.knottsgreatamericasettlement.com. A final approval hearing is scheduled for March 30, 2027. Until then, the agreement remains subject to the court's decision.

The settlement comes as Travis Kelce's reported ambassador and investor ties to Six Flags draw attention to the business.

Joel Embiid went down hard in the closing seconds of the first half as the Sixers chased the Celtics on Tuesday night. Article Title: Sandpapergate row: 'Not going to answer that' - Usman Khawaja cancels media interviews after Pat Cummins question
Article Text:
Usman Khawaja (Getty Images)

Khawaja refuses to answer question about Pat Cummins

What did Khawaja claim about Sandpapergate?

What punishments did Smith, Warner and Bancroft receive?

Khawaja denies making claims to boost book sales

Cricket Australia responds to fresh allegations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography, Sabr. The move follows a tough interview in which he was questioned about his claims surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate.News Corp reported that publisher Penguin informed media outlets about the cancellations on Wednesday morning. This came after Khawaja faced questions from Sarah Ferguson on ABC's 7.30.Khawaja is reportedly concerned that his future interviews will focus mainly on the ball-tampering controversy rather than the other subjects covered in his book.During Tuesday's interview, he had already indicated that he did not want to discuss the allegations any further."I've talked on social media about this and I've written in my book, that's my statement, that's what it is, and I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment in time," he said.During his conversation with Ferguson, Khawaja was asked about Warner backing his version of events and his statement that any "lies will eventually get out"."What lies is he talking about?" she asked."I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey," Khawaja replied."I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment."Khawaja said he wanted the entire team to accept responsibility for the incident rather than leave three players to face the consequences."All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team, and I don't think that's a lot to say. I'm not asking a lot from people and I say, 'We were a part of it. That was us'. Let's just take accountability. I was here to tell my truth, what I saw, what I felt, and to stick with those three guys who were made out to be the only people who have taken it [accountability]," he said.Ferguson also asked Khawaja whether Australia captain Pat Cummins knew about the use of sandpaper. However, the former opener did not answer the question."I'm not going to answer that."He added: "I've written what I've written in my book. I've come out and stood by those three guys and told my account of what I saw."Cummins, along with fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, had publicly denied knowing about the incident in 2021.Khawaja sparked a fresh debate on Saturday by claiming that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the 2018 Test against South Africa in Cape Town. His statement is different from Cricket Australia's findings at the time, which held Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft responsible for knowing about the plan before it was carried out.He also claimed that sandpaper had been used in the previous Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha."It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he said ahead of the release of his book.Khawaja, who retired this year after playing 88 Tests, has devoted an entire chapter of his autobiography to the scandal.The Cape Town scandal had serious consequences for Smith, Warner and Bancroft. All three players were sent home following the incident. Smith received a 12-month ban and lost the Australia captaincy. Warner was also banned for 12 months and removed from leadership positions, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.Khawaja believes the outcome might have been different if the entire team had accepted responsibility."I don't believe the whole team would have got a ban if we went in together," he said."I think it would have been shared. It's very hard to ban the whole team."Khawaja also rejected suggestions that he had made the revelations now to attract more buyers for his autobiography.He told Ferguson that the ball-tampering issue was not part of the discussion when he signed his publishing deal in 2023. He also said his manager and publisher found out about the chapter only six months ago."Even when I gave it to them six months ago, they were shocked because I don't really talk about this to anyone," he said.The former Australia opener also explained why he chose to share his account after retiring from international cricket."The reason I felt more comfortable saying it now is because I don't speak for the team anymore," he said."If I try to come out and do it while I'm still on the team, they have to look at me every day. We have to go operate as a team."Cricket Australia has responded to Khawaja's claims and defended the findings of its investigation. However, it also accepted that the inquiry was completed within a short period."The three players who received bans after the Cape Town Test acknowledged their breaches and accepted the penalties imposed," a spokesperson told Nine newspapers."We have acknowledged that the investigation was conducted in a short timeframe given the impending Test match and that there are varying opinions about some matters including the length of the sanctions imposed. We respect that players have different recollections of events from this time."But we remain comfortable the investigation's findings accurately reflect the statements and evidence provided at the time."Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has ruled out reopening the investigation.
Article Summary: Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography. The move follows a tough interview in which he was questioned about his claims surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate. He is reportedly concerned that his future interviews will focus mainly on the controversy.

NEW DELHI: Lee Fortis, who worked as Surrey's head groundsman for more than a decade, has left the club after facing disciplinary proceedings over his conduct.The club had sent Fortis on indefinite leave in late July after he had an argument with an England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) employee. The incident happened a day before MI London took on London Spirit in The Hundred at the Oval.Fortis also had a strong exchange with Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy, a former South Africa fast bowler, soon after the incident. His LinkedIn profile now shows that he left the club in October and is "open to work".A Surrey spokesperson told Telegraph Sport: "Lee Fortis has left the club and we wish him well for the future."Fortis had also been in the news in 2025 after an argument with India head coach Gautam Gambhir. The two had a disagreement over the Oval pitch. He won the top award at the ECB's Grounds Manager of the Year Awards three years in a row, from 2022 to 2024. The trade between Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh was made official on Wednesday (November 11). As part of the process, the two IPL franchises exchanged Expression of Interest (EOIs) and paperwork was submitted to the BCCI on Monday."In a marquee player trade ahead of the TATA IPL 2027, Mumbai Indians (MI) captain Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings (PBKS), while Arshdeep Singh, India’s leading wicket-taker in T20 Internationals, will join the five-time champions," read IPL's official statement."Pandya will join PBKS at a fee of Rs 18 crore, up from his existing fee of Rs 16.35 crore, while Arshdeep will join MI at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore," the statement further added.Pandya is involved in an IPL trade for the second time in three years. Ahead of the 2024 season, Mumbai Indians had brought him back from Gujarat Titans in an all-cash deal and named him captain in place of Rohit Sharma — the man who led the franchise to five titles.The homecoming was meant to give MI a long-term leader and a match-winning all-rounder. In his three seasons in charge, MI finished bottom of the table in 2024, reached the playoffs in 2025, and slipped into inconsistency again in 2026.Overall, MI won just 15 of the 39 matches under his captaincy since 2024, losing 24.His win-loss ratio (0.625) for MI is the poorest for any captain to have led a team in at least 30 IPL games. It is a sharp contrast to his record with GT — 22 wins and nine defeats in 31 games. That ratio of 2.444 ranks among the best in IPL history, just behind RCB’s Rajat Patidar, who has a ratio of 2.500 from 28 matches.At PBKS, Pandya is unexpected to hold the captaincy duties which have been firmly established by Shreyas Iyer. Over the last two IPL seasons, Iyer has been the leader of the pack and it has earned him the T20I captaincy and ODI vice-captaincy. Yet, Pandya's experience could add considerable value to PBKS, who are still vying for their first-ever title, having made two finals in 19 years, in 2014 and 2025.Meanwhile for MI, after IPL 2026, MI's need for a quality new-ball partner for Jasprit Bumrah had become abundantly clear. Trent Boult had an underwhelming season and featured in only five matches. Even if MI choose to release Boult, Arshdeep Singh would give them a ready-made replacement — another bowler capable of operating across all phases, like Bumrah.It will be Arshdeep’s first IPL stint away from Punjab Kings. Since debuting for them in 2019, the left-arm seamer has taken 111 wickets in 96 matches at an economy of 9.18.
Article Summary: Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings complete marquee player trade. Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings, while Arshdeep Singh will join MI. Pandya is involved in an IPL trade for the second time in three years. He was brought back from Gujarat Titans in an all-cash deal.

Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building one of the greatest careers in NFL history. But retirement did not mean he was ready to walk away from football. The seven-time Super Bowl champion found another way to stay connected to the league by investing in the Las Vegas Raiders. What initially looked like a $110 million business move has turned into an eye-catching financial story. With the franchise now valued at $10.3 billion, Brady's 5% ownership stake could be worth approximately $515 million on paper, highlighting the growing financial appeal of NFL team ownership.Tom Brady's journey into NFL ownership was not an overnight decision. His interest in becoming part of the Raiders organization first emerged in 2023, when he began working towards acquiring a minority stake in the franchise.The deal eventually reached its biggest milestone in October 2024. NFL owners unanimously approved Brady and businessman Tom Wagner's purchase of a combined 10% interest in the Raiders. The two investors agreed to pay $220 million, giving each of them a 5% share.According to Sports Business Journal, the transaction also involved an additional payment of approximately $24 million, known as a relocation-related fee or flip tax, connected to the Raiders' move from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020.The investment valued the franchise at around $3.5 billion for the transaction.For Brady, the agreement marked a major change in his relationship with professional football. He had spent years competing against the league's best teams. Now, he had a financial interest in one of its franchises.His personal investment of approximately $110 million also gave him a new business opportunity after his playing career. Rather than limiting his involvement to television appearances and commercial partnerships, Brady became part of the ownership structure of an NFL team.NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell welcomed the move when the league approved the agreement."It's great that Tom Brady wants to invest in the NFL," Goodell said.The approval came after months of discussions among league officials and team owners. It also cleared the way for Brady to begin his next chapter in professional football.The biggest development in Brady's ownership story is the remarkable rise in the Raiders' estimated value.When the franchise received approval for the ownership transaction in 2024, Forbes valued the team at approximately $6.7 billion. At that valuation, Brady's 5% stake would have represented an estimated $335 million.However, the latest Forbes NFL team valuations, calculated in September 2026, place the Raiders at $10.3 billion. The franchise recorded a reported 34% increase in value over one year, making it one of the most valuable teams in professional football.Applying that valuation to Brady's 5% ownership interest produces an estimated figure of $515 million.That is a substantial difference from his original investment of approximately $110 million. The implied increase stands at roughly $405 million.However, the figure needs some context. Forbes uses enterprise value, which includes equity and net debt, in its team valuations. Therefore, the $515 million figure is an illustrative estimate based on the franchise's valuation, not a confirmed market price for Brady's ownership interest.He has not publicly announced a sale of his stake, either. The increase represents estimated value on paper rather than money he has collected.Still, the numbers show why NFL ownership has become an attractive long-term investment for wealthy individuals.Brady's entry into the Raiders ownership group came with an unusual challenge. He was also preparing to work as Fox Sports' lead NFL game analyst.The situation raised questions about a possible conflict of interest. As a minority owner of one team, Brady could potentially have access to sensitive information about other franchises through his broadcasting work.The NFL addressed those concerns by placing restrictions on his media responsibilities in August 2024.According to the Associated Press report published by NFL.com, Brady could not attend in-person or online broadcast production meetings. He was also prohibited from accessing other teams' facilities, players and coaches.These restrictions mattered because NFL broadcasters often meet players and coaches before games. They also visit training facilities and attend practices to gather information that helps them prepare their coverage.Brady had to work around those limitations while beginning his broadcasting career alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt.The league also required him to follow rules governing public criticism of officials and other teams. He remained permitted to call Raiders games, but his ownership position meant that his role as an analyst came with additional responsibilities.The arrangement was unusual for someone with Brady's football experience. He had spent decades studying opponents, understanding coaching decisions and preparing for major games. Now, some of the traditional access available to broadcasters was off limits.Despite the restrictions, the NFL eventually approved his ownership bid unanimously, allowing him to continue both roles under the league's conditions.The financial growth of the Raiders is only one part of the story. Brady's involvement also brings considerable football experience and public attention to the organization.Raiders majority owner Mark Davis has an opportunity to benefit from Brady's understanding of the game. The former quarterback spent 23 seasons in the NFL, winning seven Super Bowls with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.His experience could prove useful as the franchise works towards long-term stability, particularly at the quarterback position.The Raiders have also benefited from their move to Las Vegas, where Allegiant Stadium gives the organization access to a major entertainment and tourism market. The team's commercial appeal, revenue streams and brand recognition all contribute to its rising valuation.Forbes' September 2026 figures place the franchise's revenue at approximately $887 million, with operating income of $191 million. Those numbers offer further insight into why the Raiders have become such a valuable NFL property.Brady also brings a familiar face to the franchise's growing business profile. His success on the field, media presence and commercial partnerships have made him one of the most recognisable figures in American sports.His Raiders investment therefore represents more than a financial interest in a football team. It gives him a chance to influence the sport from a different position.After years of chasing championships as a quarterback, Brady now has a different challenge. His estimated $110 million investment could be worth around $515 million based on the Raiders' latest valuation. Whether that paper gain grows further will depend on the franchise's future performance and the changing economics of the NFL.
